calibration solved from GCPs surveyed 23 Jan (not the lidar). Search envelope from the MAR lidar so the Jan lidar comparison stays independent. 24 Jan left out: the cameras were moved ~5.7 m and turned ~15 deg that day (CACO04 from 24 Jan 23:00 UTC). EARLIER CHECK (pointing_fix_figure.py on the REAL photos of Jan 18-23, before survey_products.py; these same CACO03_*_20250123 GCP calibrations, unfiltered, NO setup; PARTLY-CIRCULAR itself: its search envelope was placed with this same Jan lidar through the earlier lidar-fitted pointing): lidar elevation - water level at the waterline +0.46 m for c1 (NMAD 0.19) and +0.15 m for c2 (NMAD 0.23). Positive there = the lidar beach lies above the level the line was given: the lines read LOW, waterline - Jan lidar c1 -0.46 m, c2 -0.15 m, the sign a line without setup must have. With C = 0.037 (~0.28 m setup that week) each line rises by the share of its setup it keeps once re-projected landward, which depends on the date, the camera and the beach (0.6-0.8 in the builds so far; each build gives its own per camera, from its paired C = 0 sensitivity): expect waterline - Jan lidar of about c1 -0.29 to -0.24 m, c2 +0.02 to +0.07 m (c1 -0.18, c2 +0.13 m if all of it counted) unless the new envelope changes the detections; a 0.3 m difference between the cameras over the same hours points at the pointing or the lens model. The real photos are on the NUC only: the real numbers come from running this product there.
